cues.en: Salt. It doesn't get much attention lately, as the most that is said about it is usually just to eat less of it. But is that always the best advice? A March 1940 paper by Lawson Wilkins in Baltimore describes a case of a child who, starting from 11 months of age, had a very unusual craving for salt. In a letter responding to questions regarding their child's special appetite, the parents explained how the child would throw up almost everything except for mother's milk. At the advice of a doctor, the parents tried giving the child crackers.
cues.zh: 盐。它近来没得到多少关注，因为关于它最常说的通常只是少吃点。但这总是最好的建议吗？1940年3月，巴尔的摩的 Lawson Wilkins 在一篇论文中描述了一个病例：一个孩子从11个月大开始，对盐有非常不寻常的强烈渴望。在一封回复关于孩子特殊食欲问题的信中，父母解释说，这孩子几乎吃什么都会吐，唯独母乳除外。在医生的建议下，父母试着给孩子吃饼干。

cues.en: He threw those up too, but soon he started just licking all the salt off of the crackers and then would ask for more. Once the boy figured out what was in the salt shaker, the mother said he refused to eat anything unless the salt shaker was also on the table. He ate the plain salt by dipping his finger into it and bringing it to his mouth. It was estimated that the child was eating an extra teaspoon of plain table salt a day in addition to his foods already being saltier than his parents. Based on weight, the adult equivalent of that would be about 20 to 30 grams of extra salt per day.
cues.zh: 他把那些也吐了，但很快就只是把饼干上的盐全舔掉，然后还要更多。母亲说，男孩一旦弄明白盐瓶里装的是什么，就拒绝吃任何东西，除非盐瓶也放在桌上。他会把手指伸进普通盐里蘸着吃，再送进嘴里。据估计，这个孩子每天除了吃的食物本来就比父母更咸之外，还额外吃下了一茶匙普通食盐。按体重换算，成人相当于每天多摄入约20到30克盐。

cues.en: American Dietary Guidelines, by the way, advised people to limit their daily salt intake to a maximum of only 5.75 grams. Later, it was found out that this massive craving for salt wasn't just a quirk of the palate. The child's body was urging him to get what it needed. He was admitted to the hospital at age 3, and unfortunately after only 7 days on the hospital's low-salt diet, he suddenly died.
cues.zh: 美国膳食指南建议人们把每日盐摄入量限制在最多5.75克。后来人们发现，这种对盐的强烈渴求并不只是口味上的怪癖。孩子的身体在催促他摄取自己所需的东西。他3岁时住进医院，不幸的是，在吃医院的低盐饮食仅仅7天后，他就突然去世了。

cues.en: The final paragraph of this paper says, As this case illustrates, we can't live without enough salt. But of course, healthy people can survive on far less than what this child needed.
cues.zh: 这篇论文的最后一段写道：正如这个案例所示，没有足够的盐我们就无法生存。但当然，健康人维持生存所需的盐远少于这个孩子所需的量。

cues.en: In 2005, the U.S. federal government's dietary guidelines set a maximum limit for sodium at 2300 milligrams, or about 5.75 grams of salt per day. This is about as much sodium as is in just one and a half large-deal pickles. It was estimated that reducing Americans' intake of salt by a half teaspoon a day, about 2.8 grams, would prevent 92,000 heart attacks and save the country $20 billion in healthcare-related costs.
cues.zh: 2005年，美国联邦政府的膳食指南将钠的摄入上限设为2300毫克，约合每天5.75克盐。这大约只相当于一根半大号酸黄瓜所含的钠。据估计，美国人每天少吃半茶匙盐（约2.8克），就能预防9.2万次心脏病发作，并为美国节省200亿美元医疗相关成本。

cues.en: Their logic behind this is relatively straightforward. In large amounts, sodium pulls fluid from the body's tissues and into the blood, which raises the blood volume and the heart pumps harder. The result, high blood pressure. Chronic high blood pressure stresses the heart and arteries leading to heart disease, so less salt should mean less disease. Now, hypertension is currently at an all-time high. One in three Americans have it, but it's salt to blame.
cues.zh: 这背后的逻辑相对直接。大量摄入钠会把液体从身体组织拉进血液，使血容量升高，心脏泵血更费力。结果就是高血压。慢性高血压会给心脏和动脉带来压力，导致心脏病，所以少吃盐就应该少得病。如今，高血压发病率正处于历史最高水平。三分之一美国人患有高血压，但这该归咎于盐。

cues.en: Dietary salt intake used to be far higher than it is now, mainly out of necessity. Before the industrial era, salt was the most common and effective food preservative. As Mark Kerlansky points out in Salt A World History, we know that the salt intake in Europe was very high, at least from the 1500s, when it was as much as 40 to 100 grams, thanks to food like salted fish. This amount would be like consuming the entire contents of one to two, two ounce salt shakers like you'd see in a diner.
cues.zh: 过去膳食盐摄入量远高于现在，主要是出于必要。工业时代之前，盐是最常见、最有效的食品防腐剂。正如 Mark Kerlansky 在 Salt: A World History 中指出的，至少从16世纪起，欧洲的盐摄入量就非常高，得益于咸鱼等食品，当时可达40到100克。这个量相当于吃下一到两个2盎司盐罐的全部内容，就像你在餐馆里看到的那种。

cues.en: If these massive quantities of salt were causing hypertension-induced heart disease, then people at the time must not have cared much about sudden death, considering the first report of heart disease didn't occur until the mid-1600s. Then, from the early 1800s until the end of World War II, Western societies consumed between 15 and 17 grams of salt per day, based on military archives data.
cues.zh: 如果如此大量的盐会导致高血压引发的心脏病，那么当时的人想必不太在意猝死，毕竟心脏病的第一份报告直到17世纪中叶才出现。随后，从19世纪初到二战结束，根据军事档案数据，西方社会每天摄入15到17克盐。

cues.en: After World War II, when refrigeration began to displace salt as the main means of food preservation, salt consumption in the US dropped dramatically to about half that rate, or 9 grams, 1.8 teaspoons per day, and, based on 24-hour urinary sodium data, has remained flat for the last 50 years. So, despite this historically low and steady salt intake, prevalence of hypertension is now three times as high as it was in the first half of the 1900s.
cues.zh: 二战后，冷藏开始取代盐成为主要的食物保存手段，美国盐摄入量大幅下降到约此前的一半，即每天9克、1.8茶匙；根据24小时尿钠数据，过去50年一直保持平稳。因此，尽管盐摄入量处于历史低位且稳定，如今高血压患病率却是20世纪上半叶的三倍。

cues.en: So, salt intake is still high, according to health guidelines, but this doesn't explain how hypertension keeps going up while salt consumption stays steady. The South Koreans eat a wide variety of salty foods, with the easiest example being kimchi, cabbage, and other vegetables preserved in salt and spices. Kimchi is eaten at literally every meal. The average South Korean consumes around 4,000 milligrams of sodium per day, almost twice as much as the US dietary guidelines recommend.
cues.zh:
所以，按照健康指南，盐摄入量仍然偏高，但这无法解释为什么盐摄入量保持稳定，高血压却持续上升。
韩国人吃种类繁多的咸味食物，最简单的例子是泡菜，以及用盐和香料腌制的卷心菜和其他蔬菜。
他们每顿饭都吃泡菜。
韩国人平均每天摄入约4000毫克钠，几乎是美国膳食指南推荐量的两倍。

cues.en: Despite this, South Korea has the lowest rates of coronary heart disease in the world, according to 2014 data from the World Health Organization. In fact, the data from a September 2015 paper funded by the Korea Food Research Institute shows that the quartile groups that consumed the most sodium had the lowest rates of hypertension, coronary heart disease, and stroke.
cues.zh: 尽管如此，根据世界卫生组织2014年的数据，韩国冠心病的发病率全球最低。事实上，韩国食品研究院资助的2015年9月一篇论文的数据显示，钠摄入量最高的四分位组，高血压、冠心病和中风的发病率反而最低。

cues.en: This has been dubbed the Korean paradox, and as Dr. James De Nicole Antonio points out, you could swap out Korea for any one of 13 other countries, and get a lot more paradoxes regarding high salt intakes. In his very thorough book, The Salt Fix, Dr. De Nicole Antonio makes the case that reducing salt intake is not only unnecessary, but potentially harmful to health.
cues.zh: 这被称为“韩国悖论”。正如 James De Nicole Antonio 博士所指出的，把韩国换成其他13个国家中的任何一个，都会在高盐摄入方面得到更多悖论。在他非常详尽的《The Salt Fix》一书中，James De Nicole Antonio 博士论证说，减少盐摄入不仅没有必要，还可能有害健康。

cues.en: Salt has several very important functions. It's needed by the heart to pump blood properly, it's needed by the stomach to facilitate digestion, and it is necessary for bone formation and bone strength. It's a key component in cell-to-cell communication and the optimal transmission of nerve impulses to and from organs like the heart and brain. As is explained in the Washington Manual's endocrinology subspecialty consult, at particularly low sodium levels,
cues.zh: 盐有若干非常重要的功能。心脏需要盐来正常泵血，胃需要盐来促进消化，骨骼形成和骨骼强度也离不开盐。它还是细胞间通讯的关键成分，也是神经冲动在心脏、大脑等器官之间最佳传导的关键成分。正如《Washington Manual》内分泌专科咨询分册所解释的，当钠水平特别低时，

cues.en: Patients may present with neuropsychiatric signs and symptoms ranging from muscular weakness, headache, lethargy, ataxia, and psychosis to cerebral edema, increased intracranial pressure, seizures, and coma. On the other side of the spectrum, consuming particularly large quantities of salt can of course have terrible consequences.
cues.zh: 患者可能表现出神经精神体征和症状，从肌无力、头痛、嗜睡、共济失调和精神病，到脑水肿、颅内压升高、癫痫发作和昏迷。另一方面，摄入特别大量的盐当然也可能带来严重后果。

cues.en: According to a 1913 article in the Zhejiang Province and probably in other provinces of China, the drinking of a saturated solution of salt was a common mode of committing suicide. People would down an entire pint to pint and a half of saturated salt solution. They usually drank the brine used for pickling cabbage. But for it to kill someone, all this salt had to be consumed very quickly in order to overcome the powerful filtration ability of the kidneys.
cues.zh: 根据1913年浙江（可能还有中国其他省份）的一篇文章，喝饱和盐水是一种常见的自杀方式。人们会一口气喝下一品脱到一品脱半的饱和盐水。他们通常喝的是腌白菜用的卤水。但要致人死亡，必须非常快地喝下所有这些盐，才能压过肾脏强大的过滤能力。

cues.en: This is why 16th century Europeans could consume so much salt. While 100 grams of salt is a massive amount, it can simply be processed by the kidneys if ingested at a normal pace. So if humans had to consciously restrict their salt intake in order to stay healthy, this would suggest that our regulating systems like the kidneys aren't very powerful at all. But our history suggests otherwise.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么16世纪的欧洲人能摄入那么多盐。虽然100克盐是很大的量，但如果按正常速度摄入，肾脏完全可以处理。所以，如果人类必须刻意限制盐摄入才能保持健康，那就说明像肾脏这样的调节系统根本不够强大。但我们的历史表明并非如此。

cues.en: In order for our cells to work properly, systems had to develop that could regulate the concentration of salt and other components of our blood and extracellular fluid. The kidneys, of course, are very important in this respect. Considering cells can't survive outside a narrow range of electrolyte levels in the extracellular fluid, the ability to retain salt, and at the same time excrete excess salt, is very important. Mammals who get their food from the sea such as the sea lion, sea otter, walrus, and polar bear in just large amounts of salt.
cues.zh: 为了让细胞正常工作，必须发展出能调节血液和细胞外液中盐及其他成分浓度的系统。肾脏在这方面当然非常重要。考虑到细胞只能在细胞外液电解质水平很窄的范围内存活，保留盐分、同时排出多余盐分的能力非常重要。从海洋获取食物的哺乳动物，比如海狮、海獭、海象和北极熊，会摄入大量盐。

cues.en: But the salt content of their blood is not very different from that of terrestrial mammals. From our perspective at least, these animals' kidneys must be able to excrete massive quantities of salt. But the basic physiology of the kidneys is the same in humans. Through the process of osmoregulation, the water and sodium levels in our body are constantly balancing each other out.
cues.zh: 但它们血液中的盐含量与陆生哺乳动物相差不大。至少在我们看来，这些动物的肾脏必定能排出大量盐分。但人类肾脏的基本生理机制也是一样的。通过渗透调节，我们体内的水分和钠水平始终相互平衡。

cues.en: If the blood sodium levels drop too low, water from the blood will enter our tissues to maintain this balance. When there's an increase in sodium in the blood, the kidneys simply excrete the excess into our urine. As is explained in the book The Salt Fix, if our blood and fluid levels of sodium get high, we start reabsorbing less salt from the kidneys and absorb less salt from the foods we eat. The liver can signal the intestine to reduce sodium absorption.
cues.zh: 如果血钠水平降得太低，血液中的水分就会进入组织，以维持这种平衡。当血液中的钠增加时，肾脏会直接把多余的钠排入尿液。正如《The Salt Fix》一书所解释的，如果血液和体液中的钠水平升高，肾脏就会减少对盐的重吸收，我们也会从食物中吸收更少的盐。肝脏可以向肠道发出信号，减少钠的吸收。

cues.en: And if sodium begins to accumulate, our bodies also tend to harmlessly shunt excess sodium to the skin or organs. In fact, a 1979 paper authored by Frederick Luft and colleagues described an experiment where they gave people with normal blood pressure various amounts of sodium, going as high as 87 grams of salt. They found that the urinary sodium excretion approached the total sodium intake at each level. Their bodies were simply excreting these excess loads of salt.
cues.zh: 当钠开始积累时，我们的身体也会倾向于把多余的钠无害地分流到皮肤或器官。事实上，Frederick Luft 及其同事在 1979 年的一篇论文中描述了一项实验：他们让血压正常的人摄入不同量的钠，最高达到 87 克盐。他们发现，在每个摄入水平上，尿钠排泄量都接近钠的总摄入量。他们的身体只是在排出这些过量的盐负荷。

cues.en: to the point that they were able to excrete 10 times a normal sodium intake, up to 86 grams of salt per day. Dr. Danico-Lontonio points out that these kinds of capabilities suggest that the human body is well adapted to handle salt overload, but not salt deficit. So if it's easier for the body to handle excess salt rather than insufficient salt, we should expect to have data showing higher rates of mortality from lower salt intake. Well, this data is available.
cues.zh: 以至于他们能排出相当于正常钠摄入量10倍的钠，每天多达86克盐。Danico-Lontonio 博士指出，这些能力表明人体很适应处理盐过量，却不适应缺盐。所以，如果身体处理盐过量比处理盐不足更容易，我们就应该预期有数据表明较低盐摄入量的死亡率更高。嗯，这样的数据确实存在。

cues.en: A 2014 article in the New England Journal of Medicine analyzed the mortality and cardiovascular event rates of 102,000 people assessed for urinary sodium and then followed them for 3.7 years. The article concluded that an estimated sodium intake between 3 grams and 6 grams per day was associated with a lower risk of death and cardiovascular events. But what's important is that the adverse effects to health increase much more rapidly when you are under this range rather than above it.
cues.zh: 2014年《新英格兰医学杂志》的一篇文章分析了10.2万人的死亡率和心血管事件发生率，这些人接受了尿钠评估，随后被随访3.7年。文章结论是，每天钠摄入量估计在3克到6克之间，与较低的死亡风险和心血管事件风险相关。但重要的是，当低于这个范围时，健康的不良影响上升得比高于这个范围快得多。

cues.en: As you go over 6 grams of sodium, about 15 grams of salt, the health risk does start to rise, but it rises much more gradually. Based on the data here, eating 6 times as much salt as is recommended by the US Dietary Guidelines would pose less of a risk to your health than actually following the guidelines. Animals have a very strong innate drive to acquire salt specifically, just like they would go to great lengths to acquire water or food when thirsty or hungry.
cues.zh: 当你摄入超过6克钠（约合15克盐）时，健康风险确实会开始上升，但上升得平缓得多。根据这里的数据，摄入量达到美国膳食指南推荐盐量的6倍，对健康造成的风险反而比真正遵循该指南还小。动物有一种非常强烈的先天驱动力，会专门去获取盐，就像它们在口渴或饥饿时会不惜一切代价获取水或食物一样。

cues.en: Elephants will uproot entire trees to get at the salty soil under the roots. Gorillas will chew on rotting wood to eat the salty microbes, and some animals will drink urine due to its sodium content. But these efforts pale in comparison to what humans have done for salt. Mark Kolanski's book Salt a World History is a 449 page testament to this, as he shows salt-seeking drove civilization, built empires, and won wars. Romans established every major city near a saltworks, and for some time Roman troops were paid in salt.
cues.zh: 大象会连根拔起整棵树，只为吃到树根下含盐的土壤。大猩猩会啃腐木，吃含盐的微生物；有些动物还会因为尿里含钠而喝尿。但这些与人类为盐做过的事相比，简直不值一提。Mark Kolanski 的《Salt: A World History》厚达449页，正是这一点的见证：他展示了寻盐如何推动文明、建立帝国、赢得战争。罗马人把每座主要城市都建在盐场附近，有一段时间罗马军队的军饷就是用盐支付的。

cues.en: Britain lost control of its American and Indian colonies when it lost control of their salt supplies. Kirlansky states, the history of the Americas is one of constant warfare over salt. Whoever controlled salt was in power. When salt is freely accessible, people across many populations tend to consistently consume between 3,000 and 4,000 milligrams of sodium per day. In America, the country infamous for reckless eating habits, from 2011 to 2012, the average daily sodium intake was only 3,600 milligrams.
cues.zh:
英国失去对美洲和印度殖民地盐供应的控制时，也就失去了对这些殖民地的控制。
Kirlansky 指出，美洲的历史就是一部围绕盐的持续战争史。
谁控制了盐，谁就掌握权力。
当盐可以自由获取时，许多人群每天摄入的钠往往稳定在3000到4000毫克之间。
在因饮食习惯放纵而闻名的美国，2011至2012年日均钠摄入量仅为3600毫克。

cues.en: This suggests that the body will push people to acquire salt, but in accordance with their actual needs for the mineral. In a 1936 paper titled Experimental Sodium Chloride Deficiency in Man, through seven days of sweating and sodium-free diets, subjects became sodium deficient. The participants reported that they experienced extreme unquenchable thirst. One participant reported that he experienced a longing for salt and often went to sleep thinking about it.
cues.zh:
这表明，身体会促使人们获取盐，但会依据人对这种矿物质的实际需求。
在1936年一篇题为《人体实验性氯化钠缺乏》的论文中，受试者通过七天出汗和无钠饮食，出现了钠缺乏。
参与者报告称，他们经历了极度且无法缓解的口渴。
一名参与者报告说，他渴望盐，常常想着盐入睡。

cues.en: With regard to mood-related symptoms, subjects reported a loss of appetite, anhedonia, difficulty concentrating, excessive fatigue, and a general sense of exhaustion. A 1995 study at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine was done on a group of chronic fatigue syndrome patients. Patients were encouraged not to restrict sodium intake and were given the drug fludrocortisone, which causes the body to retain sodium.
cues.zh: 关于情绪相关症状，受试者报告了食欲下降、快感缺失、注意力难以集中、过度疲劳以及一种整体的精疲力竭感。1995年，约翰斯·霍普金斯大学医学院针对一组慢性疲劳综合征患者开展了一项研究。研究鼓励患者不要限制钠摄入，并给他们服用氟氢可的松，这种药会让身体潴留钠。

cues.en: 76% of the patients reported a favorable response to this therapy by manifesting reduced chronic fatigue syndrome symptoms and improved clinical signs. Especially noteworthy was the observation that the patients also improved scores on a test of general well-being that likely reflected improved mood. At the conclusion of the study, it was learned that 61% of the chronic fatigue syndrome patients had voluntarily imposed low sodium diets upon themselves.
cues.zh:
76%的患者报告对该疗法反应良好，表现为慢性疲劳综合征症状减轻、临床体征改善。
尤其值得注意的是，患者在一项总体健康感测试中的得分也有所提高，这可能反映了情绪的改善。
研究结束时了解到，61%的慢性疲劳综合征患者自行采取了低钠饮食。

cues.en: As the 17th century's Chinese scientist and encyclopedias Song Yingxing said, There are in the world five tastes. A man would not be unwell if you abstain for an entire year from either the sweet or sour or bitter or hot, but deprive him of salt for a fortnight and he will be too weak to tie up a chicken. Craving for salty foods is surely not indicative of salt being addictive, but just shows that the body has an impressive ability to drive you to consume what it needs.
cues.zh: 正如17世纪中国科学家、百科全书式学者宋应星所说：世间有五味。人若整年不碰甜、酸、苦、辣中的任何一味，都不会不适；可要是两周不给他盐，他就会虚弱得连鸡都绑不住。渴望咸食当然不说明盐会成瘾，只说明身体有一种惊人的能力，能驱使你摄入它所需的东西。

cues.en: A 1928 study in the American Journal of Diseases of Children found that when very young normal children were given free access to a variety of natural foods to choose by themselves, they selected foods that facilitated normal growth and development. There was even one child with rickets caused by a vitamin deficiency that continued to take large amounts of straight cod liver oil over a period of 101 days. After the deficiency symptoms disappeared, so did his craving for cod liver oil.
cues.zh: 1928年发表在《美国儿童疾病杂志》上的一项研究发现，当非常年幼的正常儿童可以自由选择多种天然食物时，他们会选择促进正常生长发育的食物。甚至有一个因维生素缺乏而患佝偻病的孩子，在101天里持续服用大量纯鱼肝油。缺乏症状消失后，他对鱼肝油的渴望也消失了。

cues.en: The reason humans in general are hovering around an intake of three to four grams of sodium per day despite the World Health Organization and US government urging them to cut their salt intake down to lower than 2.3 grams a day is Probably because their bodies are pushing them to acquire the amount that is best for them
cues.zh: 尽管世界卫生组织和美国政府都敦促人们把盐摄入量降到每天2.3克以下，但人类总体上每天的钠摄入量仍徘徊在3到4克，原因很可能是身体在促使他们摄入最适合自己的量

cues.en: As mentioned earlier, a sodium intake of 3 to 6 grams, about 7 to 15 grams of salt, seems to be an ideal range for most people. However, if you're losing more salt from sweating a lot or being on a low carbohydrate diet, this range may be shifted upward to say 4 to 7 or 5 to 8 grams of sodium or more. Now, there's still several points about specifically why lowering salt intake stresses the body, contrary to conventional health advice, so stick around. I'll be covering the science behind this another time.
cues.zh: 如前所述，每天摄入3到6克钠，约合7到15克盐，似乎是大多数人的理想范围。不过，如果你因为大量出汗或采用低碳水饮食而流失更多盐分，这个范围可能会上移，比如提高到每天4到7克，甚至5到8克或更多的钠。那么，关于为什么降低盐摄入反而会给身体带来压力、这与传统健康建议相悖，还有几个要点，所以请继续看下去。我之后会再讲这背后的科学原理。
